Where an entry sits in its review life.

Only `approved` entries may be selected in a design; the others exist so
that "we looked at this" survives the person who looked.
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

CatalogEditRequest.description: An editorial edit (ADR-0062 rule 1). Omitted fields are left alone.
CatalogEditRequest.title: CatalogEditRequest

CatalogEntry.title: CatalogEntry

CatalogEvent.description: One recorded mutation of an entry: who, when, and what changed.
CatalogEvent.title: CatalogEvent

CatalogKind.description: What kind of building block an entry describes.
CatalogKind.title: CatalogKind

DataGrant.description: An agent's access to one data plane.
DataGrant.title: DataGrant

Entitlement.description: Who may select an entry, when not everyone may.
Entitlement.title: Entitlement

FigureMethod.description: How a figure got into the catalog.
FigureMethod.title: FigureMethod

FigureProvenance.description:
Where an entry's numbers came from, and when they were last confirmed.

Attached to the entry rather than to each number: a source publishes a
model's whole row at once, and per-field provenance would imply an
independence the sources do not have.
FigureProvenance.title: FigureProvenance

Harness.description:
Everything that wraps the model to make an agent operable.

A harness is the unit the designer UI edits and the unit governance
reviews: model, tools, MCP mounts, database grants, limits and policy.
Harness.title: Harness

HumanCounterpart.description:
The person an agent works for and escalates to.

Every agent has exactly one accountable human. Approval policy decides
which actions stop and wait for that person.
HumanCounterpart.title: HumanCounterpart

MCPServerRef.description:
An MCP server the agent's harness mounts.

`transport=stdio` runs a local command; `http`/`sse` connect to a URL.
Secrets are referenced by name, never inlined.
MCPServerRef.title: MCPServerRef

OperatorActionRequest.description: Why an operator acted. Recorded; not validated beyond being present.
OperatorActionRequest.title: OperatorActionRequest

OrgUnit.description: A node in the company org chart (division, department, team).
OrgUnit.title: OrgUnit

RelationalGrant.description:
Scoped relational-database access exposed through an MCP server.

The harness never hands an agent raw credentials: it hands it a named
connection whose reachable schemas/tables and statement classes are fixed
here, and the MCP server enforces them.
RelationalGrant.title: RelationalGrant

Runtime.description: Which agent framework executes the agent loop.
Runtime.title: Runtime

SandboxSpec.description: An agent's instantiation of a template, with narrow overrides.
SandboxSpec.title: SandboxSpec

SandboxTemplate.description:
A reusable, reviewed execution environment definition.

Templates are the governed boundary for agent code execution: an agent
may only run inside a template an administrator has published.
SandboxTemplate.title: SandboxTemplate

TenantRegistrationRequest.description:
What an operator supplies to mint a tenant.

The isolation domain is absent on purpose: it is derived from the prefix
by the fabric (ADR-0050), never asked for.
TenantRegistrationRequest.title: TenantRegistrationRequest

ToolBinding.description: A single callable exposed into the agent loop.
ToolBinding.title: ToolBinding

Visibility.description:
Data plane an artifact lives in.

PRIVATE    - readable/writable only by the owning agent (and its human).
PROTECTED  - shared with every agent in one or more groups.
PUBLIC     - readable by every agent in the organization; any agent may
             contribute, subject to the contribution policy.
Visibility.title: Visibility

info.description: The Agentic Designer platform API. **`/api/v1` is the public, versioned contract** (ADR-0115); the unversioned `/api/...` paths serve the bundled UI and are not described here. Identity follows the designer's auth mode (`none`, `trusted_proxy`, `oidc` — ADR-0047, ADR-0114); every designer route goes through the same service layer and RBAC whichever client calls it (ADR-0018). A Python client is `orgagents.client`; the MCP servers are `orgagents mcp designer|runtime`. See docs/DEVELOPERS.md.
info.title: Organizational Agentic System

get.description:
Where each agent's work lives, and what may cross. Reads only.

A placement is an org unit crossed with an environment class
(ADR-0069) — the namespace model an enterprise already has. What is
drawn from this is a *region*, so it must be the thing that compiles:
`agents` is who shares a volume and a process namespace, and `rules` is
the whole of what crosses. Everything absent is denied.

A placement is **not** a security boundary. The tenant is (ADR-0050).
The response says so rather than leaving a reader to infer it from a
picture of boxes.

schema.title: Response Designer Placements V1 Api V1 Designer Systems  System Id  Placements Get

get.summary: Where each agent's work lives, and what may cross. Reads only.

could not put to the platform at all.

post.description:
Ask the fabric to run a design, or say exactly why it refused.

The designer **requests**; it does not deploy. The deployment is
created in `requested`, and the fabric compiles it for real and moves
it on under its own authority (ADR-0049). Two reasons, both load
bearing: the tenant is assigned by the fabric and never named by a
design, because a design that could name its own tenant could widen
its own boundary (ADR-0050); and the platform policy is the fabric's
to apply.

So what happens here is a preflight and a request. A refusal is
returned as the reason with the gate's own findings, and is written to
the audit log — a refused publish is the phase gate saying no to a
named person about a named design, and nothing else would keep that.
